chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Abd al-Aziz, from Ubayd ibn Zurarah, from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام:
Concerning a slave jointly owned by two men: one of them married him off while the other did not know of it; then later he came to know of it. Does he have the right to separate the two of them?
He عليه السلام said: The one who did not know and did not give permission has the right to separate them when he comes to know, and if he wishes, he may leave him upon his marriage.

key_terms.زَوَّجَهُ: married him off or arranged his marriage
key_terms.عَبْدٍ: a male slave whose legal status is under discussion
key_terms.لَمْ يَأْذَنْ: did not grant permission or authorization
key_terms.لَمْ يَعْلَمْ: did not know about the marriage arrangement
key_terms.نِكَاحِهِ: his marriage contract or marital bond
key_terms.يُفَرِّقَ: to separate the spouses by annulling the marriage

ai.seo_question: Can a co-owner annul the marriage of a jointly owned slave if it was done without his permission?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about a jointly owned male slave whose marriage was arranged by only one owner without the other's knowledge or permission. The Imam عليه السلام rules that the uninformed co-owner may annul the marriage upon learning of it, or may choose to let it remain in effect. The report highlights the legal significance of ownership rights and consent in marriage arrangements involving slaves.
